correctness.rationale: The discrete log-concavity half-space localization theorem reduces all linear upper-tail maxima under E[X]<=m on bounded intervals to log-affine laws on subintervals. For each interior position j on length r<=7, the mean of the truncated geometric is strictly increasing in its log-ratio parameter and so is the upper tail. All 15 rational (r,j,q0) witnesses independently recomputed H_rj(q0)>0 and D_rj(q0)<0; therefore at the exact mean-constrained optimum q*<q0 and tail<1/2. Reflection controls the lower tail; for r=1,2 integer mean forces degeneracy or the only interior cases do not arise. The given 8-point bracket H(8,5,34/25)<0<H(8,5,11/8) and D(8,5,34/25)>0 yields the exact violating log-affine law. The finite signs alone are not a proof of the localization premise, which is stated in the cited primary theorem.
